prompt:
Add an opt-in deployment inventory to MkDocs so build and serve users can obtain a trustworthy machine-readable list of the files that were actually emitted. Implement this throughout the normal config, build lifecycle, plugin API, CLI, tests and user documentation; it must not be a separate external script.

Add a build_manifest configuration option, default None, accepting a nonempty relative output path such as deployment/manifest.json. Add --manifest PATH to both mkdocs build and mkdocs serve; a supplied flag overrides YAML, while an omitted flag preserves YAML. Serve and its rebuilds must use the same build behavior. None disables the feature entirely, including its new plugin event. Keep all current defaults, command options, existing plugin ordering and dirty-build semantics compatible.

The path is relative to site_dir. Validate it through the normal configuration error mechanism: reject non-strings, empty paths, absolute POSIX or Windows paths, drive-relative paths, backslashes, empty components, . or .. components and control characters. Ordinary Unicode and spaces in valid path components are allowed. At write time, reject a destination that is a symlink or has a symlink parent; never write outside site_dir. Detect a collision with a current documentation page, copied source asset, generated File, extra template or theme template instead of overwriting that output.

After all ordinary post_build hooks have succeeded and strict-mode warnings have been checked, collect the actual regular files under site_dir, including theme assets, search output, nested files, dotfiles and files created or changed by post_build plugins. Do not traverse symlink directories or include symlink files. Exclude the manifest itself and the temporary file used to write it. For dirty builds, inventory all currently present output files, including unchanged or stale files that MkDocs intentionally leaves in place; this is a disk inventory, not a list of files rendered in the latest call.

Write UTF-8 JSON with the exact core shape {"version": 1, "files": [{"path": "guide/index.html", "size": 123, "sha256": "..."}]}. path is a unique relative POSIX path, files are sorted lexicographically by path, size is the final byte length (not character count), and sha256 is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the exact final bytes. No absolute local paths, timestamps or platform separators belong in these core fields. Empty files, binary data and Unicode names/content must be correct. Two inventories of identical file bytes must be identical without relying on mtimes. Stream large files through the digest rather than buffering an entire site in memory.

Add an on_build_manifest(manifest, *, config) plugin event, including BasePlugin and PluginCollection typing and the normal event priority/chaining behavior. It runs once per enabled successful build after the inventory has been collected and before the atomic write. As with ordinary modifying events, a hook may mutate the supplied mapping, return a replacement mapping, or return None to keep the current value. Plugins may add JSON metadata at the top level or to entries. The authoritative core inventory must remain truthful: reject changed version, missing/added/duplicate file entries, modified path/size/digest fields, non-mapping results and metadata that cannot be encoded as strict JSON, including non-finite numbers. A hook may reorder entries, but the saved manifest must retain sorted path order. Preserve metadata added by earlier hooks under the existing event chaining semantics.

Validate everything and serialize before replacing an existing manifest. Use a temporary sibling file and atomic replacement, cleaning temporary artifacts on success and failure. If a post_build hook, strict warning, manifest hook, validation or serialization fails, do not publish a new manifest; an existing manifest in a dirty build must remain unchanged. Report failures through the existing build error/plugin error handling. Manifest failures must not be silently downgraded to success. This requirement covers the manifest's publication; ordinary site outputs retain MkDocs' existing build behavior.

Add focused tests to the existing config, command/build, serve/CLI and plugin test modules, plus integration coverage for final-disk accuracy, clean and dirty builds, plugin-created/changed files, generated File collisions, search output, directory URL modes, Unicode/binary/empty files, safe relative paths and symlinks, hook chaining and invalid hook results, failure preservation and repeated deterministic builds. Update the configuration reference, CLI documentation and plugin developer documentation with runnable examples and lifecycle ordering. Run the full available project unittest suite using its existing *tests.py discovery convention and appropriate format checks, fix introduced regressions, and report remaining limitations accurately. Complete all listed interfaces, making routine implementation choices autonomously.
